title: Se me olvidó: impersonal and accidental se
summary: Impersonal se talks about what people in general do; accidental se turns a mishap into something that happened to you.
focus: Impersonal se (se vive bien) and accidental se with an indirect pronoun (se me olvidó)
content:
## The many faces of se

**Se** has more uses than any other word in Spanish. Six jobs share one form:

| use | example | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| reflexive | **Marta se lava el pelo.** | Marta washes her hair. |
| reciprocal | **Se quieren mucho.** | They love each other. |
| se for le/les | **Se lo di ayer.** | I gave it to him yesterday. |
| passive (last lesson) | **Se venden pisos.** | Flats for sale. |
| impersonal | **Aquí se vive bien.** | People live well here. |
| accidental | **Se me olvidó.** | It slipped my mind. |

This lesson covers the last two uses, **se** for people in general and **se** for things that happen to you without anyone meaning them to.

## Impersonal se: people in general

**Se** + a third-person **singular** verb, with no subject, says what people in general do (English *you*, *one*, *people*):

- **En este barrio se vive muy bien.** (Life is good in this neighbourhood.)
- **En mi empresa se trabaja mucho.** (People work hard at my company.)
- **¿Cómo se dice *mug* en español?** (How do you say *mug* in Spanish?)

With people after the personal **a**, the verb stays **singular**:

- **Se busca a los culpables.** (They are looking for the culprits.)
- Compare the passive, which agrees: **se buscan camareros.**

A reflexive verb cannot take a second **se**; use **uno**: **uno se acostumbra** (you get used to it).

## Accidental se: it happened to me

To say something went wrong **sin querer** (by accident), Spanish makes the thing the subject and names the unlucky person with an indirect pronoun:

| se + | who it happened to | verb |
|---|---|---|
| se | me / te / le / nos / os / les | olvidó, cayó, rompió… |

- **Se me olvidó tu cumpleaños.** (I forgot your birthday; it slipped my mind.)
- **Se le cayeron las llaves.** (He dropped his keys.)
- **Se nos rompió la lavadora.** (Our washing machine broke.)
- **¿Se te ha perdido algo?** (Have you lost something?)

Common verbs: **olvidarse, caerse, romperse, perderse, acabarse, estropearse, escaparse, ocurrirse**.

## Agreement and blame

The verb agrees with **the thing**, not the person:

- **Se me olvidó la cita. / Se me olvidaron las entradas.**

**Se** always comes first: **se me**, never *me se*. To name the person, add **a** + noun: **A Juan se le cayó el móvil.**

The choice tells the listener who is to blame:

- **Rompí el jarrón.** (I broke the vase, maybe **a propósito**, on purpose.)
- **Se me rompió el jarrón.** (The vase broke on me by accident.)

It works in every tense: **se nos acabó**, **se te ha perdido**, **se le había olvidado**, **que no se te olvide**.

vocabulary.meaning: they say that, it is said that
vocabulary.example: Se dice que el nuevo jefe es muy exigente.
vocabulary.example_meaning: They say the new boss is very demanding.

vocabulary.meaning: the culprit, the one to blame
vocabulary.example: Todavía no se sabe quién es el culpable del incendio.
vocabulary.example_meaning: It isn't known yet who is to blame for the fire.

vocabulary.example: Perdona, te he pisado sin querer.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Sorry, I stepped on you by accident.

vocabulary.example: No lo hizo a propósito; fue un despiste.
vocabulary.example_meaning: He didn't do it on purpose; it was a slip.

vocabulary.meaning: to slip one's mind (se me olvida)
vocabulary.example: Se me olvidan siempre las contraseñas.

vocabulary.meaning: to fall; to be dropped (se me cae)
vocabulary.example: Se le cayó la bandeja delante de todos.
vocabulary.example_meaning: She dropped the tray in front of everyone.

vocabulary.example: Se nos rompió la cafetera el lunes.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Our coffee maker broke on Monday.

vocabulary.meaning: to get lost; to go missing
vocabulary.example: Se me perdió el pasaporte en el aeropuerto.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I lost my passport at the airport.

vocabulary.example: Se nos acabó el café a media mañana.
vocabulary.example_meaning: We ran out of coffee by mid-morning.

vocabulary.example: Se les estropeó el coche en plena montaña.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Their car broke down right in the mountains.

vocabulary.meaning: to get away; to slip out
vocabulary.example: Se me escapó una carcajada en la reunión.
vocabulary.example_meaning: A laugh slipped out of me in the meeting.

vocabulary.meaning: to occur to, to come to mind
vocabulary.example: ¿Se te ocurre algún regalo para Ana?
vocabulary.example_meaning: Can you think of a present for Ana?

vocabulary.example: Se me derramó el vino sobre el mantel.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I spilled the wine on the tablecloth.

quiz.prompt: In «Se lo di a Marta ayer», what is se doing?
quiz.explanation: Before lo, la, los or las, the indirect pronoun le/les becomes se: le di el libro becomes se lo di.
hints: Who received it? Marta, so it is an indirect object.

quiz.prompt: En este pueblo ___ muy tranquilo: no hay tráfico ni ruido.
quiz.explanation: Impersonal se takes a third-person singular verb and no subject: se vive (people live).
hints: Nobody in particular lives here. It means people in general.

quiz.prompt: La policía ha dicho que ___ a los culpables del robo.
quiz.explanation: With people introduced by the personal a, impersonal se keeps the verb singular: se busca a los culpables.
hints: Look at the little word a before los culpables.

quiz.prompt: Lo siento muchísimo, ___ tu cumpleaños. (olvidar, preterite: it slipped my mind)
quiz.explanation: Accidental se: se + me (the person affected) + olvidó, agreeing with tu cumpleaños.
hints: se first, then the pronoun of the person it happened to.

quiz.prompt: A Pablo ___ las llaves en el metro.
quiz.explanation: Se comes first, le names Pablo, and the verb is plural because las llaves fell.
hints: The verb agrees with the keys, not with Pablo.

quiz.prompt: ___ la leche, así que bajé a comprar más. (acabar, preterite: we ran out of milk)
quiz.explanation: Running out is accidental se: se + nos + acabó, singular because la leche is singular.
hints: Who ran out? We did: nos.

quiz.prompt: ¿Qué buscas? ¿___ algo? (perder, present perfect, tú: Have you lost something?)
quiz.explanation: Accidental se in the present perfect: se + te + ha perdido.
hints: Use se, te, a form of haber and a participle.

quiz.prompt: Which sentence says the vase broke by accident?
quiz.explanation: Se me rompió presents the breaking as something that happened to me. Rompí el jarrón a propósito says I did it deliberately; me rompí is not how you say it about a vase.
hints: The accident makes the vase the subject.

quiz.prompt: Estaba en la ducha cuando de repente ___ una idea genial. (ocurrir, preterite: an idea came to me)
quiz.explanation: Ideas occur to you: se + me + ocurrió, singular to agree with una idea.
hints: The idea is the subject; you are the indirect pronoun.

conversations.title: One of those mornings
conversations.scenario: Diego arrives at the office an hour late and soaked; his colleague Clara wants to know what happened.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¡Diego, por fin! Aquí se empieza a las nueve, ¿recuerdas?
lines.meaning: Diego, at last! Here we start at nine, remember?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Lo sé, lo sé. Hoy se me ha torcido el día.
lines.meaning: I know, I know. Today has gone wrong for me.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Para empezar, se me olvidó poner el despertador.
lines.meaning: To start with, I forgot to set the alarm.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Bueno, eso le pasa a cualquiera.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Luego, con las prisas, se me cayó el café encima.
lines.meaning: Then, in the rush, I spilled coffee all over myself.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: No, eso fue el paraguas: se me rompió en la parada del autobús.
lines.meaning: No, that was the umbrella: it broke on me at the bus stop.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Pues anímate: aquí se trabaja mejor con un café. ¿Te traigo uno?
lines.meaning: Well, cheer up: people work better here with a coffee. Shall I bring you one?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Sí, por favor. Pero llévalo tú, por si se me cae.
lines.meaning: Yes, please. But you carry it, in case I drop it.

listening.note: Impersonal se takes a singular verb and has no subject.

listening.text: En verano se duerme fatal en esta habitación.
listening.meaning: You sleep terribly in this room in summer.

listening.text: A mi abuela se le cayeron las gafas al suelo.
listening.meaning: My grandmother dropped her glasses on the floor.
listening.note: New word: las gafas = the glasses.

listening.text: Se nos acabó la gasolina en mitad de la autopista.
listening.meaning: We ran out of petrol in the middle of the motorway.
listening.note: New word: la autopista = the motorway.

listening.text: Al llegar al cine, vimos que se nos habían olvidado las entradas.
listening.meaning: When we got to the cinema, we saw we had forgotten the tickets.
listening.note: The verb agrees with las entradas: habían olvidado.

listening.text: Sin querer, se me rompió la taza favorita de mi compañero de piso.
listening.meaning: By accident, I broke my flatmate's favourite mug.
listening.note: New word: la taza = the mug.

guide.tip: ¿Cómo se dice…? and ¿Se puede…? are impersonal se you already use every day, with no subject and a singular verb.

bites.title: Impersonal se
bites.rule: Se + a third-person singular verb, with no subject, says what people in general do: se vive bien, se trabaja mucho, ¿cómo se dice…?
bites.example: En esta ciudad se sale mucho por la noche.
bites.example_meaning: People go out a lot at night in this city.

bites.title: Se + personal a
bites.rule: With people after the personal a, impersonal se keeps the verb singular, even before a plural.
bites.example: Se entrevistó a todos los testigos.

bites.title: Accidental se
bites.rule: se + me/te/le/nos/os/les + verb. The thing is the subject and the pronoun names who it happened to.

bites.title: Se goes first
bites.rule: Always se me, se te, se le… never me se. The verb agrees with the thing: se me olvidó la cita, se me olvidaron las entradas.

sorts.title: Which se is it?

items.text: Se trabaja mucho en esta oficina.

sorts.why: Impersonal: no subject, singular verb. Passive: the verb agrees with what is sold or rented. Accidental: a pronoun (me, le…) names who it happened to.

sorts.title: Reflexive, reciprocal or se for le?
sorts.why: Reflexive: to oneself. Reciprocal: to each other. Se for le: le/les become se before lo, la, los, las.

spots.sentence: A Luis se le cayó las llaves.
spots.why: The verb agrees with the thing that fell, so las llaves takes cayeron.

spots.sentence: Se buscan a los culpables del robo.
spots.why: With the personal a, impersonal se keeps the verb singular.

spots.sentence: En este pueblo se viven muy bien.
spots.why: Impersonal se has no subject, so the verb is singular.

spots.sentence: A nosotros se nos acabaron el pan.
spots.why: The verb agrees with what ran out, el pan: se nos acabó.

spots.sentence: Se me rompí el plato sin querer.
spots.why: The plate is the subject: se me rompió, third person.

builds.text: Se me olvidó la cartera en casa.
builds.meaning: I left my wallet at home.

builds.text: En este barrio se vive muy bien.
builds.meaning: Life is very good in this neighbourhood.

builds.text: A Pedro se le cayeron los papeles.
Se busca a los testigos del accidente.
builds.meaning: They are looking for the witnesses of the accident.
